channel.title: Los Angeles Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Los Angeles Times (latimes.com)

item.title: Shohei Ohtani will not pitch for Japan in WBC: 'Just seemed like the right decision'
item.description: Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said at the team's annual DodgerFest at Dodger Stadium that Shohei Ohtani would not pitch for Japan in the World Baseball Classic.

item.title: 'National shutdown' brings protests to L.A., across the nation; demonstrators clash with police
item.description: Nationwide protests take place Friday as part of a 'National Shutdown' in response to immigration actions in Minnesota. Protesters clashed with police.

item.title: Californian tech company to move headquarters to Florida
item.description: D-Wave Quantum Inc. said it will relocate its headquarters to Boca Raton, Fla., before the end of the year.

item.title: Trump officials’ loss of credibility in ICE cases seen in court defeats
item.description: The Department of Justice has lost five cases in Los Angeles against defendants accused of assaulting immigration agents, leading former government officials to warn that the Trump administration faces a growing credibility crisis with the public.

item.title: Austin Beutner's daughter found beside a highway in Palmdale the night she died
item.description: Sheriff’s deputies responded to assist paramedics, who treated Emily Beutner, 22, at the scene.

item.title: Will Supervisor Lindsey Horvath enter the mayor's race? She's got a week to decide
item.description: Horvath, who is currently seeking re-election, said she will spend the weekend in "deep reflection" over whether to enter the race. The deadline for filing is Saturday.

item.title: LAUSD teachers union members authorize strike, ratcheting up pressure on contract talks
item.description: United Teachers Los Angeles members authorized their leadership to call a strike. Stalled talks have moved to the fact-finding stage.

item.title: New message from top Democrats: The U.S. Justice Department can't be trusted
item.description: Leading Democrats' remarks that the U.S. Department of Justice cannot be trusted hold stunning implications for American democracy, and followed a week of equally stunning actions by the department.

item.title: Demonstrations against ICE tactics continue in L.A.
item.description: Protests across the country continue throughout the weekend in response to federal immigration raids and the killings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti by immigration enforcement officers in Minneapolis.

item.title: Epstein files reveal emails between Ghislaine Maxwell, L.A. Olympics boss Casey Wasserman. He expresses regret
item.description: The latest cache of investigative files on Jeffrey Epstein includes personal emails exchanged between Casey Wasserman, chairman of the LA28 Olympics organizing committee, and convicted sex offender Ghislaine Maxwell. In a statement Saturday, Wasserman said "I am terribly sorry for having any association with either of them," adding the emails were exchanged "long before her horrific crimes came to light."
